sections.html:
Mansfield is a Tolland County town in the Capitol Planning Region. The 2020 population was 25,892, spread over 45.5 square miles, most of it land. There is no single center. The town is a collection of small settlements: Atwoodville, Eagleville, Gurleyville, Mansfield Center, Mansfield Depot, Mansfield Hollow, Mount Hope, Spring Hill and Storrs, among others.

Part of town belongs to Connecticut's Quiet Corner, the rural northeast. Two Mansfield houses can sit in very different settings and draw very different buyers.

  • Storrs: campus-adjacent, anchored by the main University of Connecticut campus, with a mixed-use downtown built in the mid-2000s.
  • Mansfield Center: mostly a bedroom community with a small business district, bordering Willimantic to the south.
  • Gurleyville, Mansfield Hollow and Atwoodville: older village areas with historic districts.

Mansfield was incorporated in October 1702 after separating from Windham, and it moved from Windham County to Tolland County in 1827. The first silk mill in the United States was built here. The Gurleyville Gristmill, dating to 1835 on the Fenton River, is the only fully intact gristmill of its kind in Connecticut.

The University of Connecticut began in 1881, when Charles and Augustus Storrs gave 170 acres and $6,000 to the state to found the Storrs Agricultural College. The Mansfield Training School, a state facility on more than 1,000 acres, operated until 1993.

The Gurleyville, Mansfield Center and Mansfield Hollow historic districts are on the National Register of Historic Places. If your house is in or near one, ask the town what that means for exterior changes before you start repairs.

The University of Connecticut dominates local employment, with 5,314 employees in the town's 2024 annual financial report. The Town of Mansfield employs 419. Natchaug Hospital and United Services each have 250 to 499, and Big Y, Price Chopper and Mansfield Nursing and Rehab have 100 to 249 each.

The effect on housing is a rental-heavy market around campus and a quieter owner-occupied market in the outer villages. A house with student tenants, an unfinished repair list or an owner who has moved away is a common situation near Storrs.

Mansfield is reached mainly by Route 195 (Storrs Road), Route 44, Route 32 and a stretch of Route 6 on its southern edge. Route 195 meets Route 44 at the intersection locals call the four corners, and Routes 44 and 32 meet at Mansfield Depot. The Route 6 freeway section is a leftover piece of a planned Hartford to Providence interstate that was never finished, and it has an interchange with Storrs Road at the Willimantic line.

  • Windham Region Transit District runs local routes 674 and 675 and the HuskyGo campus shuttle.
  • CT Transit route 913 is an express bus between Storrs and Hartford.
  • Peter Pan Bus Lines offers limited intercity service to Hartford Union Station and Providence.
  • The Nash-Zimmer Transportation Center on Royce Circle in downtown Storrs is the local hub.

Passenger rail left the area in 1955, and the nearest historic station was in Willimantic, about nine miles south of Storrs.

Mansfield Elementary School and Mansfield Middle School serve younger students, and high school students attend E. O. Smith High School, part of Regional School District 19. The former Annie E. Vinton and Dorothy C. Goodwin schools have been rebranded as campuses of Mansfield Elementary. Assignments can change, so confirm current boundaries with the schools before you quote them to a buyer.

Mansfield taxes rest on a Grand List taken each October 1. The mill rate for the 2025 Grand List is 20.00. Bills come in July and January, and the assessor's page has the current schedule.

Every five years the assessor runs a town-wide revaluation, and the most recent took effect October 1, 2024. After a revaluation, assessment notices go out and owners can appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals by the deadline set at that time. Connecticut law lets the board reduce an assessment only if the owner, an attorney or an authorized agent appears in person and is sworn in. Appeals the board declines to hear can go to Superior Court under C.G.S. 12-117a.

  • Assessor phone: 860-429-3311, closed Fridays.
  • Hours: Monday to Wednesday 8:00 a.m. to 5:15 p.m., Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.
  • Defective concrete and crumbling foundation information has its own page on the assessor site.

Bills follow the October 1 owner of record, so ask the title company how the closing statement will split the current installment between you and the buyer.

Connecticut puts the real estate conveyance tax on the seller, with one part going to the state and one to the town. Under C.G.S. 12-494, the state share on a home sale is three-quarters of one percent of the price and the municipal share is one-quarter of one percent.

ComponentRateApplies to
State share0.75%Home price up to $800,000
State share1.25%$800,000 to $2,500,000 portion
Municipal share0.25%Standard home sale

The seller, an attorney or an agent files Form OP-236 with the town clerk when the deed is recorded. The tax applies when the price is $2,000 or more, and the clerk cannot record the deed until the return is filed and the tax paid. Transfers between spouses and a principal residence sold in lieu of foreclosure are exempt, and a principal residence with a pyrrhotite foundation certified by an engineer has its own exemption on the first sale after certification. Your closing attorney will confirm what applies.

sections.h2: Who sells here and what to gather
sections.html:
Most Mansfield sellers fall into a few groups: owners of rental houses near campus, families inheriting a house in an outlying village, and homeowners with older properties needing work. An older house in the Quiet Corner can carry deferred maintenance, and a historic district adds a layer to renovation planning.

A listing means preparing the house, scheduling showings and waiting through the buyer's financing. An as-is cash sale removes those steps, and you decide whether the timing and number work for you.

  • Gather the latest tax bill and the assessor's record card for the property.
  • Confirm who holds title, especially after an inheritance.
  • Ask the town clerk's office about recording steps for your deed.
  • Ask the town about any open permits, code issues or zoning questions.

faqs.q: Is Mansfield, CT in Tolland County?
faqs.a: Yes. Mansfield is a Tolland County town in the Capitol Planning Region. It was part of Windham County until 1827.

faqs.q: When are Mansfield property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Bills follow a July and January schedule, based on the October 1 Grand List. Contact the Mansfield tax collector for the exact due dates on your bill.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Mansfield assessment?
faqs.a: File a written appeal with the Board of Assessment Appeals by the deadline set after assessment notices go out. The board can lower an assessment only if you or your agent appears in person. Appeals it will not hear can go to Superior Court.

faqs.q: What conveyance tax does a seller pay in Connecticut?
faqs.a: On a typical home sale the seller pays 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town, with a higher state rate on the part of a residential price above $800,000. Form OP-236 is filed when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Mansfield that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Mansfield houses sell as-is, either to a cash buyer or to a buyer who plans repairs. Gather your tax bill and title information first so the sale can move quickly.
